previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of psoriatic arthritis was admitted for a worsening flare involving left-sided joints—elbow, fingers, knee, and foot—over five days, despite increasing prednisone and restarting azathioprine. He also experienced significant diarrhea, which improved during admission. Due to concerns about oral medication absorption, he was treated with IV methylprednisolone and IV pain control. Stool studies were negative for infection, supporting a non-infectious inflammatory flare. His pain and gastrointestinal symptoms improved, and he was transitioned to a prednisone taper. He was discharged home with plans to start Simponi and follow up with rheumatology and gastroenterology.
problems: Secondary diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, not stated as uncontrolled, or unspecified
Unspecified hereditary and idiopathic peripheral neuropathy
Adrenal cortical steroids causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
